participants.private_seed: Every budget round lately turns into an argument over which pot the money may come from rather than what the network needs. Headline totals stopped meaning much to me once I saw what they commit us to paying in the years afterwards.

participants.name: Toshio

persona.name: Toshio

He tends to take a step back from those around him, is not very assertive, and has an air of mystery about him. Occasionally, he observes things with a sharp gaze and has the ability to quickly assess situations. As a result, he is trusted by others as a reliable presence, but he is cautious about getting deeply involved with others. It seems that he has experienced some pain or suffering in his past, but he rarely shows it to others, and those scars may be connected to his cold-hearted side.

participants.private_seed: Ever since the reorganisation, the schemes that stall are never the ones we expected to stall, and the cause is never anything written in the drawings. Before believing any delivery date now, I want to know who else has to say yes and what the ground might hide.

participants.name: Takumi

participants.private_seed: Institutional memory here is short: the same ideas come back every decade and nobody looks up what happened last time. What I have started doing is reading the closure reports before the enthusiasm sets in.

## Setting
Selection of a transit improvement plan for a metropolitan authority. Five reviewers appointed by a metropolitan transit authority deliberate over the improvement plans prepared for the network. - Contingency pricing inside the pre-war shells
- Joint operators' committee minutes
- Completion records of the earlier accessibility programme

- Timed runs and crowd counts mid-city
- Journey audits on where minutes go
- Roster books for the late-turn pool
- Crew establishment and maintenance contract

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Victoria, Takumi, Toshio, Daisuke and Sakura. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |

## Your profile
Name: Victoria
Age: 37
Gender: female
Personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: Plans here are written as if the people to run them will simply appear, and the same handful of crews end up carrying whatever we decide. Before anything is promised, I would rather know which rosters already have nothing left in them.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The participants introduce their priorities for the investigation. They discuss the need to look at historical data, staffing levels, and financial commitments.
- Round 2: Participants share the implications of their findings without revealing the full text. They debate the feasibility of different types of improvements based on staffing, budget, and historical success.
- Round 3: The participants evaluate the candidates against the discovered constraints. They weigh the available budget and staff against the projected impact on passengers before voting.

Each participant's part:
- Victoria: Cares about the availability of personnel to operate the plan. She examines roster capacity and maintenance contracts to ensure the plan is staffable.

- Two pilots from eight years ago
- Timed runs and crowd counts mid-city
- Journey audits on where minutes go
- Roster books for the late-turn pool
- Crew establishment and maintenance contract

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Victoria, Takumi, Toshio, Daisuke and Sakura. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

Name: Victoria
